newsitem.title: USA: U.S. offers missile defense funds to Israel.
newsitem.headline: U.S. offers missile defense funds to Israel.

text.p: The United States on Thursday offered to provide more financial aid to help Israel speed development an anti-missile defence, including extra funds for the Arrow missile and a high-energy laser weapon.
The announcement was made by Pentagon spokesman Ken Bacon shortly after talks between visiting Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai and U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen.
"The details aren't totally worked out, but we will increase our investment in the Arrow missile programme and (the investment) will help with testing and other aspects of it," said Bacon.
He said current U.S. aid for the Arrow programme, which stands at about $200 million over five years, might be increased by as much as 25 percent after consultation with Congress.

Bacon gave no additional financial figures, but said the United States had also offered to provide more money for joint work on the U.S. "Nautilus" high-energy laser, which Israel hopes to use against Katyusha rockets of the type fired into northern Israel from southern Lebanon last year.
Israel is currently developing the Arrow to shoot down Scud and other missiles and Bacon said that Israel considered the weapon very important to its defence.
